items.title: Palo Alto Sinks 10%, Okta Down 11% as Wall Street Dumps Software’s AI Winners
items.summary: Key TakeawaysPalo Alto Networks fell 10% today, along with Okta, as the AI sell-off hit this year’s software winners. Palo Alto went into today far above its five-year average multiple, for about 9% EPS growth in fiscal 2027.

items.title: Palantir and CrowdStrike stocks tumble as Wall Street dumps software's AI winners
items.summary: Investors are selling the software stocks that rode the AI boom and mostly sparing the ones that have been left behind.

items.title: Dan Ives Remains Bullish on Palantir Despite Sector Weakness. What This Means for PLTR Stock.
items.summary: Ives remains bullish on Palantir despite sector weakness, calling the software selloff indiscriminate and naming the company his top software pick after Q3 revenue grew 96%.

items.title: CrowdStrike Sinks 9%, Palo Alto Down 8%, Cloudflare Down 9% as AI Trade Unwinds
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCrowdStrike shares fell 10% as investors sold off AI stocks, and the company had no news to explain the drop. Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler and Cloudflare fell with it, as the market sold cybersecurity as a group.

items.title: Palantir Tumbles 10%, CrowdStrike Sinks 9% as Wall Street Dumps Software’s AI Winners; Okta Drops 10%
items.summary: Software's biggest AI winners are getting hit hardest while the year's laggards barely move. A post-midterm shift in sentiment is reshaping who gets punished, and one security name is slipping far less than its peers.

items.title: Palo Alto Networks Eyes $500 Million AI Security Deal
items.summary: Cybersecurity giants are racing to buy specialized AI-security technology.

items.title: 3 Cybersecurity Stocks To Watch With Up To 45% Earnings Growth
items.summary: As US lawmakers push the Remote Access Security Act to close loopholes around cloud access to high end Nvidia chips, digital security is moving from a background concern to a frontline policy issue. That puts companies guarding data and networks in the spotlight. This article explains why this matters now and profiles 3 cyber security stocks from a global screener with strong balance sheets and high growth expectations. items.title: Palo Alto Networks Just Dropped 13% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysPalo Alto Networks (PANW) stock fell approximately 13% in the month through November 2, closing near $352 as AI competition concerns and cybersecurity valuations pressured shares. CrowdStrike (CRWD) also faced selling pressure, although improving cybersecurity budgets could support demand for its security platform.
